bad_trip_story:
This summer I traveled to Salerno. The whole idea for the trip came after I saw a video on Instagram about a traditional celebration in the region called “A'chiena.” I was fascinated by it, so I bought tickets to go with my partner and started planning the trip around that event. I love organizing trips based on local traditions in small towns or villages, because it’s such a great way to really experience the culture from the inside.
The festival was taking place in a town called Campagna, but there weren’t any places to stay there (I checked on Booking and Airbnb), so we decided to stay in Salerno, a nearby city with plenty of options. Then we bought the train tickets. Finally, we figured out how to reach the town, and thanks to Google Maps, we found the bus that would take us there.
On the actual day of the event, we got ready to go, but suddenly realized that public transport doesn’t run on Sundays. In the end, we couldn’t make it to the celebration. The truth is, I had organized everything and looked for all the options before going, so I don’t think it was a failure in the planning. Even if I had put more effort into it, it would have been hard to discover that transportation simply doesn’t run on Sundays.
representative_trip:
What best reflects my way of traveling is a trip I took this year to Viareggio. I came across it on social media: a carnival in an Italian city with gigantic floats, music, and street food. As soon as I saw it, I told my friends to see who was up for going. For me, traveling isn’t just about visiting cities, it’s also about being part of local celebrations, festivals, and traditions. That’s why, whenever I explore a new city, I usually try to go when there’s some kind of event happening.
Several of my friends joined in, and we started planning the trip together. First, we bought the event tickets to get the Early Bird discount. Then we looked for a place to stay, since there were many of us and we needed something affordable that could fit everyone. We couldn’t find anything suitable in Viareggio itself, so we decided to turn it into a weekend trip: first stop in Pisa to explore the city, spend the night there, and then head to Viareggio early in the morning to enjoy the festival. Once we found accommodation in Pisa, we booked it and bought the train tickets.
From my point of view, traveling is less about checking places off a list and more about living moments that connect me to the culture, the people, and the joy of being there at the right time.

advice_step_1: Always double-check transportation details – not just the route, but also the schedules, weekends, and holidays. It can save you from surprises like finding out too late that buses don’t run on Sundays.
advice_step_2: Stay flexible in your plans – things won’t always go as expected, so leave room for alternatives. Sometimes what seems like a setback can turn into a chance to discover something new.
advice_step_3: Balance planning with spontaneity – prepare the essentials (tickets, accommodation, must-see events) but don’t over-plan every moment. The best memories often come from the unexpected experiences in between.
destination_list_choice:
When I organized my last vacation, I did start with a small list of possible destinations. I usually like to consider a few options and then see which one feels the most exciting or meaningful at that moment. For my trip to salerno this summer, I narrowed it down by looking at the kind of experiences I wanted to have—whether it was cultural events, food, nature, or simply a chance to disconnect.
Last year, there was one destination I ruled out. It was a bigger, more touristic city where I knew I could easily spend my time, but it didn’t feel right for me. I wasn’t looking for a “classic tourist trip”; I wanted something that connected me with local traditions and gave me a sense of belonging, even if just for a few days. That’s why I said to myself, “No, this one is not for me,” and I focused on places that matched the kind of travel experience I truly enjoy.
info_saturation: I felt I had “enough” information to decide once I knew the essentials were covered: the dates of the event, how to get there, and where we could stay. For me, once those three points are clear, I usually stop searching, because I know the trip is already taking shape and I don’t want to get stuck in endless comparisons. What made me stop was a mix of practicality and excitement. I had found an option that worked logistically and also sparked enthusiasm, so there was no real need to keep digging deeper.
missing_factor:
Something that definitely influenced my decision is the people I was traveling with. For me, the company shapes the trip just as much as the destination. When I know friends are excited to join, it makes the idea of going even more appealing. Traveling with others means sharing not only the logistics but also the emotions, the laughter, and the little challenges along the way.

Another factor was my own curiosity for traditions and authentic cultural experiences. I tend to choose destinations where I feel I can connect with the local identity, not just see the “postcard version” of a place.

The whole idea for the trip came after I saw a video on Instagram about a traditional celebration in the region called “A'chiena.” I was fascinated by it, so I bought tickets to go with my partner and started planning the trip around that event. I love organizing trips based on local traditions in small towns or villages, because it’s such a great way to really experience the culture from the inside.
The festival was taking place in a town called Campagna, but there weren’t any places to stay there (I checked on Booking and Airbnb), so we decided to stay in Salerno, a nearby city with plenty of options. Then we bought the train tickets. Finally, we figured out how to reach the town, and thanks to Google Maps, we found the bus that would take us there.
On the actual day of the event, we got ready to go, but suddenly realized that public transport doesn’t run on Sundays. In the end, we couldn’t make it to the celebration. The truth is, I had organized everything and looked for all the options before going, so I don’t think it was a failure in the planning. Even if I had put more effort into it, it would have been hard to discover that transportation simply doesn’t run on Sundays.. What best reflects my way of traveling is a trip I took this year to Viareggio. I came across it on social media: a carnival in an Italian city with gigantic floats, music, and street food. As soon as I saw it, I told my friends to see who was up for going. For me, traveling isn’t just about visiting cities, it’s also about being part of local celebrations, festivals, and traditions. That’s why, whenever I explore a new city, I usually try to go when there’s some kind of event happening.
Several of my friends joined in, and we started planning the trip together. First, we bought the event tickets to get the Early Bird discount. Then we looked for a place to stay, since there were many of us and we needed something affordable that could fit everyone. We couldn’t find anything suitable in Viareggio itself, so we decided to turn it into a weekend trip: first stop in Pisa to explore the city, spend the night there, and then head to Viareggio early in the morning to enjoy the festival. Once we found accommodation in Pisa, we booked it and bought the train tickets.
From my point of view, traveling is less about checking places off a list and more about living moments that connect me to the culture, the people, and the joy of being there at the right time.. Choosing the place. When i travel normally i go to 1 city and the to places around. So decide exactly where i'm going.. Once decide it, If I need to buy any ticket, buy them. If not, i will start looking for places to book the place to stay.. Once I have the place, I buy the plane/train tickets.. Find what to do there. Go to ChatGPT, google rcomentations, civitatis, travelrrs blogs, to find the best options and to be eficient.. Be aware of travel/transport options. If you don't have your own mobility, before going to a place you have to be sure you will be able to move around.. Recommendations. I always check what other people experienced. Just to be sure, I will not lose time going to places that are not worth it at all, and it's just a tourist trap.. Accommodation availability. Maybe some people prefer to go to a place and see where to stay, that's ok, but just to be sure, check if the place has plenty of options, if not, better to book in advance.. Always double-check transportation details – not just the route, but also the schedules, weekends, and holidays. It can save you from surprises like finding out too late that buses don’t run on Sundays.. Stay flexible in your plans – things won’t always go as expected, so leave room for alternatives. Sometimes what seems like a setback can turn into a chance to discover something new.. Balance planning with spontaneity – prepare the essentials (tickets, accommodation, must-see events) but don’t over-plan every moment. The best memories often come from the unexpected experiences in between.. When I organized my last vacation, I did start with a small list of possible destinations. I usually like to consider a few options and then see which one feels the most exciting or meaningful at that moment. For my trip to salerno this summer, I narrowed it down by looking at the kind of experiences I wanted to have—whether it was cultural events, food, nature, or simply a chance to disconnect.
Last year, there was one destination I ruled out. It was a bigger, more touristic city where I knew I could easily spend my time, but it didn’t feel right for me. I wasn’t looking for a “classic tourist trip”; I wanted something that connected me with local traditions and gave me a sense of belonging, even if just for a few days. That’s why I said to myself, “No, this one is not for me,” and I focused on places that matched the kind of travel experience I truly enjoy.. I felt I had “enough” information to decide once I knew the essentials were covered: the dates of the event, how to get there, and where we could stay. For me, once those three points are clear, I usually stop searching, because I know the trip is already taking shape and I don’t want to get stuck in endless comparisons. What made me stop was a mix of practicality and excitement. I had found an option that worked logistically and also sparked enthusiasm, so there was no real need to keep digging deeper.. I usually choose medium-length trips. Sometimes, when i can i also do short trips but  it feels a bit rushed, you barely arrive, and it’s already time to leave. Very long trips require more time off and more resources, which isn’t always possible. A medium-length trip gives me the perfect balance: enough time to immerse myself in the culture, take part in local events, and explore beyond the main attractions, but still short enough to stay practical and manageable with my studies and work

bad_trip_story: I’m not entirely dissatisfied with my recent trip to Istanbul, but I know I could’ve made it better. I didn’t plan enough, so most of my time ended up in souks and malls, when I could have explored more unique local spots. This experience taught me that while spontaneity has its charm, I shouldn’t leave my trips completely unplanned. A bit of structure helps ensure I cover the experiences that matter most to me.
representative_trip:
I had a wonderful vacation in Djerba for many reasons. First, everything was organized by an agency; they handled the accommodation, transportation, activities, and more. That took away the usual mental burden I face when planning a trip myself.

Second, the destination itself was truly fascinating. Even though I’m from Tunisia, the south is very different from the north, so visiting a place where I didn’t know exactly what to expect was refreshing. I discovered an authentic city, enjoyed time at the beach, and shared quality moments with my family. At the same time, I explored the cultural side of Djerba through the Guellala Museum, local events, and concerts.

One highlight was visiting the Ghriba Synagogue. It was my first time in a synagogue, and it gave me insight into Judaism and its history in Tunisia. And of course, no trip is complete without food: I loved trying the local street food and desserts, which added so much flavor (literally!) to the whole experience.
scene_1: I arrive at my accommodation; a small but authentic place that feels both cozy and refined. The bed is inviting, the view is stunning, and every little detail is thoughtfully prepared.
scene_2: I step outside to find good weather, the kind where the sun is shining even in winter. The scenery is naturally beautiful, and it makes me want to stay outside all day.
scene_3: Later, I sit down at a local restaurant where the scent of spices and freshly prepared dishes fills the air. The plates are vibrant and flavorful, each bite a discovery of authentic cuisine, served with care and generosity.
scene_4: I walk through a city that’s easy to explore on foot. From one spot to the other I bounce with excitement, each corner has something new to discover.
best_story_choice: I compare 3–4 destinations, read reviews, and book after a few days (Comparo 3–4 destinos, leo reseñas y reservo después de unos días)
decisive_info: Free cancellation is a reassuring thing to have. If I change my mind, I can always cancel.
choose_step_1: First, decide what kind of vacation you want. Do you imagine yourself chilling at a hotel, sleeping in and reading by the pool? Or do you want an active trip where you wake up early, move from one place to another, and discover as much as you can? Defining the vibe of your vacation is the foundation.
choose_step_2: Next, start collecting recommendations both online and offline. Search for destinations that match the type of vacation you picked, but don’t stop at the first Google results. Dig deeper to find underrated spots that are less crowded and more authentic. And don’t forget to ask friends or family who might have tips and personal experiences to share.
choose_step_3: Finally, build a plan that fits your budget. Leave a little room for unexpected expenses, and book things in advance. That way, once you arrive, your only responsibility is to follow the plan and enjoy your vacation stress-free.
advice_step_1: Invest in your comfort. That cheap early flight might look like a good idea at first, but losing sleep and spending your first day exhausted isn’t worth it. Choose options that keep you rested and energized.
advice_step_2: Don’t leave planning for when you’re already on vacation. Figuring things out on the spot eats up time you could be enjoying. Do the work beforehand so you can fully relax once you’re there.
advice_step_3: Always stay connected. Get a local SIM card or make sure you have internet access, and download a translation app if you don’t speak the language. Being over-prepared is always better than being caught unprepared.
destination_list_choice: My last planned vacation was actually quite random, so I didn’t really start with a clear list of destinations. Instead, I considered different options as they came up and evaluated each one on the spot. It was less about crossing places off a list and more about asking myself, "Does this destination make sense for me right now?" In the end, I chose the one that felt the most convenient and exciting at that moment.
info_saturation: I usually feel I have enough information once a destination fits my budget, matches my interests, and has positive recommendations from people I trust. At that point I stop searching because it feels good enough to make a decision. If I had more time I would probably look deeper into local experiences, hidden gems, or cultural events that are not always easy to find in a quick search.
missing_factor: One thing that usually influences my decisions is the opportunity to learn something new. Whether it’s history, local traditions, or even trying a completely new activity, I’m drawn to destinations where I can come back having experienced or understood something I didn’t know before.

trip_length_choice: I usually choose short to medium trips because they are affordable and easier to plan around my days off and other commitments.

bad_trip_story: The latest trip that I was not satisfied with I had packed too many things in the itinerary, because I had too few days to spend. I paid for a city tour and wasn't able to make it in time, and I didn't have any other days available to be able to do the specific tour. If I were to do it again, I would try to pick more realistic scheduling.
representative_trip: I recently visited Portugal (Porto & Lisbon) and I think it reflects the way I like to travel the most. The trip consisted in renting a car for cross-country traveling, but picking locations where I was able to walk around or use public transport for most of my needs. This way I felt like I was actually living and experiencing the city, as opposed to hopping on the car all the time and spending too much time within the vehicle.
scene_1: Understanding budget I have available.
scene_2: Deciding on a location I want to visit, usually based on places I've always wanted to visit, or things I've seen online, and understanding the mediums to get to said place.
scene_3: Deciding what I want to do in this place, and building out a preliminary itinerary. Will usually rely on chatgpt or google to see itinerary suggestions to make the best out of it.
scene_4: Deciding if there are places close to this place in order to make the best out of the travel to see things that are closeby.
best_story_choice: I compare 3–4 destinations, read reviews, and book after a few days (Comparo 3–4 destinos, leo reseñas y reservo después de unos días)
decisive_info: Reviews. I feel like 320 reviews is enough of a base to trust the review, and 4.6 to me is way better than 4.2.
choose_step_1: I would highly suggest comparing reviews for hotels and other things that compose a large portion of the experience. Google maps is very helpful to understand locations, proximity to what you're looking to visit, reviews, and just general high level planning.
choose_step_2: I would highly suggest to rely on AI/LLM/ChatGPT-like solutions for itinerary for the first pass of things to do. It will save you time from collecting infromation throughout the web, and will also organize your thoughts in ways that make sense for your trip.
choose_step_3: I would make sure you go into it with a budget or amount of money you are willing to spend. The idea of travelling is enjoying it fully, but if you're constantly second guessing whether or not to spend money, you're not enjoying it fully. Seperating a chunk of money that you are willing to spend ensures that whether you spend 10 or 100 of that, it's all within what you were ok with spending.
advice_step_1: Think beforehand which are your must-sees and nice-to-see locations and plans. That way you can course correct easily if your itinerary was too ambitious.
advice_step_2: Search enough beforehand so you don't return from the vacation thinking you wish you new because you woud have visited it.
advice_step_3: Don't trust instagram travel posts entirely.
destination_list_choice: I did. I made my final choice based on how much money and time I had. I didn't visit places that I didn't think I would have enough time to visit fully, because it wouldn't make sense to spend the time going there.
info_saturation: When it starts becoming frustrating. If I had more time I would find people that have visited the places in the past and wrote down their suggestions.

representative_trip: A trip I took to southern Chile — the Lake District and Patagonia — I chose it because I like connecting with nature, seeking authentic experiences. I researched, read travel blogs, asked people; I was interested in landscapes and local culture, so I prioritized destinations like Chiloé and Torres del Paine, where I could try typical foods, go trekking — those are my ideal trips, the ones where I can explore calmly.
scene_1: The city noise fades away after hours in the car and a walk through green trails, you arrive at a wooden cabin by a lake, take out your notebook and write; real silence, the breeze moves the leaves, and an old man is fishing. scene_3: Sleeping in that cabin so isolated from everything — the silence and being with yourself is indescribable
